data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Treating the workspace as a causal broadcast medium where every write emits a content-hash witness into a Merkle DAG shifts reclamation from a liveness test to a data-availability query; safety is preserved if and only if the protocol durably records the root hash of the problem-specific witness subtree and a quorum certificate before any reclamation decision.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The DAG has no liveness guarantee because witness nodes can crash before propagating the subtree root.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Quorum assumptions are violated by correlated failure of witness nodes during the holder crash.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The reclaimer cannot verify DAG reachability within bounded time, causing indefinite workspace retention.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The holder asynchronously publishes workspace state transitions as Merkle leaves; completion is marked by sealing the subtree root into a globally visible DAG node. The reclaimer queries DAG reachability rather than process status. The required durable record is the set of DAG root hashes witnessed by a quorum of reclaimer-adjacent nodes, ensuring that even if the original holder crashes without a terminal local record, the evidence persists in the DAG fabric.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
